## Purpose

Reconcile a completed parent repair that advanced the published aggregate after
child collection, when the original close recorded its lineage but omitted the
proof connecting it to the receipt chain. Original child receipts remain intact.

## When a playbook uses it

A local operator or the owning live supervisor previews and applies this recovery
after diagnosing a checkpoint mismatch. Normal repair closes record their own
extension automatically. An agent worker cannot authorize recovery of another task.

## How it works internally

The handler in `src/commands/integration_commands.py` authenticates operator
authority. `ParentHeadRecovery` in `src/integration/parent_repair_heads.py` locks
the project and current episode, then proves the exact stage subject, completed
delegate (including an archived delegate), latest passing completion and original
fenced close audit. It checks the current reservation, holds and pending writes.

The retained Git repository is fetched, and the actual origin ref must equal the
supplied head. The commit range must match the stage's audited repair history and
descend from the collected aggregate, preserving every receipt tip. Apply repeats
these proofs under the locks and requires the previewed episode, generation, stage
and current fence. The result reports attempts, deadline and stage/operation state.

## Side effects and persistence

Apply appends a `parent_head_extensions` edge to the original stage dossier,
including its authoring identity and operator recovery reason. It advances
`task_integration_checkpoints.checkpoint_sha` and clears current aggregate
verification. `ParentCompletion.readiness_on` consumes this edge alongside the
immutable receipts. Episode, generation, repair policy, attempts and deadlines
retain their values. No Git push or writer allocation occurs. Replay rechecks the
proof and preserves any verification recorded after the first application.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`changed` means the previewed identities or locked proof changed; preview again
and inspect the change. `blocked` reports missing authoring evidence, a mismatched
remote or lineage, unfinished collection, active writer, unresolved external
write, open gate, manual pause or human-required operation. Resolve that blocker
through its supported controls. Recovery supplies no check pass or gate approval.

## Operator example

```bash
aq integration recover-parent-head OPERATION --head FULL_COMMIT_SHA --json
```

Inspect a `would_recover` response and use its exact `apply_command`, which binds
the observed episode, generation, stage and fence. After `recovered`, run the
normal aggregate verifier for this exact head and complete through the existing
completion gates. See the incident-specific acceptance procedure in
[the design](../../superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-parent-repair-heads-design.md).
